title: Observability mesh orchestration: routing tracing hooks, metric/log pipelines and adaptive pager curation
creator: Priya Desai
description: Add a lightweight observability mesh layer that standardizes tracing hooks at the ingress/router layer, normalizes latency + error metrics downstream, and enables an adaptive pager curation layer that reduces noisy alerts while preserving SLO fidelity. This ticket covers: (1) tracing enrichment and propagation conventions, (2) transformations in metrics/log pipelines for consistent latency histograms and error signatures, (3) anomaly detection integration for SLO burn-rate adjustments, and (4) paging policy automation (dedup, signature clustering, quiet-hours & weighted on-call). Goal: reduce alert noise by 40% for runtime-related SLO breaches and make tracing + metrics usable for per-route SLA attribution.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks instrumented at ingress and router services; spans include standardized tags: route, model, version, shard_id, token_count, latency_bucket
Metrics pipeline produces 50/95/99 latency histograms and per-route error rates in the timeseries store (queryable in the console)
Alerting pipeline can perform signature-based deduplication (>=80% reduction for identical stack traces) and still page on unique SLO degradations
Adaptive pager rules implemented: severity mapping (SLO burn-rate -> paging level), quiet-hours suppression, and weighted-responder selection based on oncall load
Anomaly detector integrated with burn-rate calculator; it suppresses transient spikes (<=3m) and escalates sustained regressions (>10m) per policy
Dashboards created for latency decomposition, per-route SLO scoreboard, and alert noise KPIs with links in the runbook

End-to-end test: synthetic probe injected to mimic a 95th percentile latency regression triggers a single deduplicated incident, pages correct rotation, and creates a trace+metric link in the incident
design_decisions: Use Envoy filter layer for initial tracing hooks to avoid changing every service; inject route/model tags at the gateway

Metrics ingestion will use histogram buckets emitted from proxies and be transformed in the metrics pipeline (Prometheus remote_write -> Cortex-like store) rather than relying on client-side summaries
Signature dedup will be implemented using an L1 fingerprint (service+error_type+top_stackframe) and optional L2 clustering (minhash over stack hashes) to balance recall and precision
Anomaly detection will run in the metrics pipeline as a lightweight seasonal decomposition + robust z-score for real-time suppression; heavier ML models reserved for offline analysis
Pager curation uses a weighted-responder algorithm that factors in oncall capacity, recent paging frequency, and incident severity — avoids strict round-robin to reduce burnout
implementation_notes: Edge changes: Envoy filter that reads x-trace, enriches spans with route/model metadata and emits token_count metrics (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/134)

Collector changes: Add span enrichment pipeline stage in our Tempo-compatible collector to attach runtime tags and forward to trace store (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/612)
Metrics pipeline: add transform rules to generate histogram time-series from bucketed counters and emit per-route 50/95/99 summaries
Logs: update Vector pipeline to parse structured error fields, generate a canonical error_signature field used by dedup clustering
Alerting: extend BurnRateCalculator service to consume anomaly suppression signals and output escalations with dedup signatures
Runbook: add incident templates and drill steps for paged SLO breaches, with automated trace/metric attach links
Telemetry volume estimate: +3% cardinality from new tags (route, model) — recommended retention config change: short-term 14d high-res + 90d low-res
Backwards compatibility: collectors will accept enriched spans but should not break older spans; fallback to route=unknown when header missing
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy Envoy filter and collector changes to staging and one small production region (15% traffic)
Phase 2 (observability-on): enable metric transform and anomaly suppression for canary region, verify alerting behavior on synthetic probes
Phase 3 (expand): roll the collector and filter to all regions, enable signature dedup with conservative thresholds for 2 weeks
Phase 4 (tuning): adjust burn-rate thresholds by route tier, tune clustering recall to hit >80% dedup without losing distinct incidents
Rollback: default to 'legacy' pipeline flags that bypass enrichment and suppression if we see missing telemetry or regressions
